routes.description: Establish consciousness as the sole fundamental ontology and explain objective order, individual perspectives, causality, and nonspatiotemporal structure as configurations of universal subjectivity.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if a consciousness-only ontology avoids emergence while accounting for empirical regularity, external reality, differentiated subjects, causal efficacy, and structured relations without fundamental spacetime.

motionBridge.description: Show that consciousness is a more parsimonious and explanatorily complete ontological foundation than non-conscious matter or neutral primitives.

centralBridges.description: Explain how an observer-independent and scientifically ordered world can consist of external mental states represented through perception.
Explain individual selves and experiences as differentiated modes or excitations of one universal subjectivity.
Ground causal regularity in intrinsic properties and interactions within a single mental ontology.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect physics, neuroscience, altered experience, and consciousness theory to predictions or implications consistent with idealism.
Account for fundamental structure through semantic or cognitive relations that do not require spatial or temporal extension.

routes.description: Deny that failures of materialist emergence establish idealism by developing a neutral representational alternative and testing whether idealism explains structure, causality, and subjecthood.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if neutral representational processes avoid the hard problem while consciousness-first language fails to add necessary explanatory content concerning ordered structure, causal agents, or experience.

motionBridge.description: Show that avoiding matter-to-consciousness emergence does not require treating consciousness as the ontological foundation of reality.

centralBridges.description: Locate phenomenal character in representations without positing either separately existing physical objects or universal consciousness as substance.
Require an account of how representations, organism boundaries, and predictable order arise rather than merely labeling their inaccessible substrate mental.
Determine where causal efficacy resides when the ordinary personal self is constructed, unstable, or absent.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish correlations or mappings involving integrated information from an explanation of why subjective experience exists.
Test whether theories framed through brains, fields, vibrations, or processes can accommodate experience without ordinary space and time.

sectionSelections.title: Ontological foundation and empirical warrant
sectionSelections.rationale: The motion turns first on whether consciousness is the most economical fundamental given and whether available empirical considerations distinguish that proposal from a neutral alternative.

proSelections.proposition: Consciousness is the sole pre-theoretical given and therefore the most parsimonious foundation for reality, whereas emergence from non-conscious physical quantities supplies no intelligible explanation of experience.
Quantum measurement results, selected neuroscientific theories, and richer experience during reduced brain metabolism provide empirical considerations consistent with idealism.

conSelections.proposition: Although matter-to-consciousness emergence creates a genuine hard problem, analytic idealism does not yet explain the world's ordered structure or justify its dissociation model, so neutral monism remains preferable.

sectionSelections.title: External reality and explanatory structure
sectionSelections.rationale: A consciousness-first ontology must preserve an observer-independent ordered world and specify how perception, organisms, and regularities arise within its single category.

proSelections.proposition: Analytic idealism preserves a mind-independent external world by treating it as external mental states whose physical appearance is a perceptual representation rather than the represented reality itself.

A single mental ontology removes the unnecessary category that creates the hard problem, while dissociation, mental causation, natural selection, and intrinsic dispositions can account for organisms and predictable physical order.

conSelections.proposition: Calling an inaccessible representational substrate mental neither explains its structure nor identifies how representations are constructed, and thus appears to add no explanatory content.

sectionSelections.title: Representation, self-models, and experience
sectionSelections.rationale: The distribution of phenomenal character across representations and the status of the personal self determine whether neutral representation suffices or still presupposes consciousness.

proSelections.proposition: Self-representations and illusory personal agents are compatible with idealism, but materialist illusionism generates a regress because every neural model still requires an account of why it is experienced.

Ego dissolution leaves experience intact, and integrated information theory supports the view that informational complexes excluded from the narrative self can retain their own subjective perspectives.

conSelections.proposition: Neutral monism can avoid the hard problem by locating phenomenal character in a system's self-representation rather than in a separately existing physical object such as a bat.
Phenomenal character should extend beyond the unstable self-model to representations throughout a cognitive hierarchy, including simple and fleeting lower-level models.

sectionSelections.title: Integrated information and explanatory scope
sectionSelections.rationale: Integrated information bears on the persistence and causal role of experience, but its relevance depends on whether it supplies operational prediction, metaphysical explanation, or limited ontological implications.

proSelections.proposition: At its operational level, integrated information theory maps measurable substrate states to reported experience and makes predictions without purporting to define consciousness metaphysically.
Although integrated information theory is compatible with materialism, its account of causal complexes and existence-for-itself gives it limited idealist implications.

conSelections.proposition: Integrated information theory's correlation between integrated information and degrees of consciousness does not explain why there is anything it is like to be a system.

sectionSelections.title: Subjecthood and the source of causality
sectionSelections.rationale: The ontology must identify the bearer and source of causal efficacy when personal selves are modeled as constructed and dream contents may arise without an experienced agent.

proSelections.proposition: Experiences are excitations of a universal core subjectivity rather than separable contents, and individual selves are modes of that single underlying subjectivity.
Causality arises from the intrinsic archetypal properties and natural self-excitation modes of the one universal field of subjectivity.

conSelections.proposition: Assigning causal power to the dreaming subject remains unclear if the self is not what it appears to be and the imagined object lacks causal power.
The green-elephant example still fails to locate causality because an ordinary non-lucid dream need contain no distinct self that causes its represented contents.

sectionSelections.title: Structure without fundamental spacetime
sectionSelections.rationale: The account of fundamental reality must preserve differentiation and meaningful structure even when ordinary spatial and temporal organization is absent or nonfundamental.

proSelections.proposition: Idealism can preserve nature's structure without spacetime by treating fundamental structure as semantic or cognitive relations whose meaning requires no extension.

conSelections.proposition: Experiences in which time and space disintegrate raise doubts about their fundamentality and challenge explanations that implicitly presuppose spatiotemporal processes.
